StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Single and the sim leaves Power.on_stack alone, so it adds -- which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236, no StackType branch). This is the CORRECT handling of Single; the census's 15 wrong units are the ones that override on_stack to `pass` (`py audit/tools/power_census.py stack`). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterDeath.issue: Right hook and the right two spawns (`CreatureCmd.Add<SneakyGremlin>` then `<FatGremlin>`, SurprisePower.cs:23-24, vs powers.py:1704-1706 in the same order, which matters because it fixes the enemy-list indices). The gap is the THIEVERY TRANSFER. C# iterates `base.Owner.GetPowerInstances<ThieveryPower>()` -- plural, because ThieveryPower is per-target -- and for each one creates a HeistPower with `heistPower.Target = powerInstance.Target` and applies `DynamicVars.Gold.IntValue` with `applier: base.Owner` (SurprisePower.cs:26-33). The sim reads a single `self.owner.powers.get("thievery")` and applies one HeistPower with `thievery.gold_stolen` and NO applier (powers.py:1707-1709). Three divergences in one: (a) one instance instead of N -- power_cmd gap G5's InstancedPerApplier/Instanced collapse, and ThieveryPower is per-Target so the game really can hold several; (b) no Target on the HeistPower, so the sim cannot say whose gold it is; (c) the missing `applier=`, the same shape as power/high_voltage's. DORMANT in Ironclad scope for (a) and (b) -- one player means one Thievery target -- and dormant for (c) by the executed applier-reader enumeration. Also absent: `GremlinMercNormal.MarkGoldStolen()` (SurprisePower.cs:34-37), which the sim does not call; that is the encounter's record. **BLOCKED DEPENDENCY worth naming:** both ThieveryPower and HeistPower are among the four ported powers missing from ALL_POWERS (main report section 8 item 1), so they cannot be audited through the harness at all -- this unit's correctness rests on two units nobody can record. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldStopCombatFromEnding.issue: No sim counterpart. C# reads this through Hook.ShouldStopCombatFromEnding at CombatManager.cs:196, inside the win check: while any power returns true the combat cannot end. `hooks.py` defines no such hook and combat.py:272-277 decides the win purely from `is_gone` over the non-minion enemies. The sim reaches the same OUTCOME here by the mid-death spawn / death prevention described on this record's death entry, which keeps `_all_enemies_dead()` false on its own, so DORMANT -- but the mechanism is absent, and a future power wanting to hold combat open without also adding a creature or preventing a death would have nothing to hook. Third-file citations, not hashed here. ENGINE-LEVEL HOME (added 2026-07-26): this mechanism now also carries `gap` at audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json step 8c, which owns the missing hook surface itself; same verdict at every site per rule 3.

guards.what: powers.py:1703 passes `combat._rng` for the spawn's HP roll
guards.rationale: The sim passes `combat._rng` -- the shared LEGACY random.Random -- to the spawned monster's constructor (powers.py:1703), and Monster.__init__ rolls the spawn's HP from it (monsters/base.py:78-79 `hp = rng.randint(self.min_hp, self.max_hp)`), where the game rolls a mid-combat spawn's HP on a NAMED stream. Half A found seven power units reaching for `combat._rng` where C# names a stream, so this was checked as a systematic class rather than trusted: the sim REPAIRS it one level up. `CreatureCmd.add` calls `combat.assign_parity_hp(creature)` (cmds.py:254 -> combat.py:259-267), which re-rolls a mid-combat spawn's HP on the **Niche** stream against the current siblings, mirroring CombatState.CreateCreature's SetUniqueMonsterHpValue -- and it is a no-op in legacy mode, where the shared rng IS the model. The Sneaky/Fat Gremlin really does have HP variance (min_hp 10, max_hp 17), so the repair is load-bearing rather than vacuous. Faithful, with the caveat that the constructor's `randint` still consumes a draw from the unseeded shared rng in parity mode -- harmless, because no parity content reads that stream. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

`wasRemovalPrevented: true` is passed when Hook.ShouldDie returned FALSE, i.e. when the DEATH was prevented (CreatureCmd.cs:566), and `false` on the real-death path (CreatureCmd.cs:519) -- the parameter is misnamed in the decompiled source and is NOT about ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath (computed separately at CreatureCmd.cs:508). So `!wasRemovalPrevented` means "the creature actually died". The sim fires hooks.on_death ONLY on the should_die-returned-True branch (cmds.py:98-105) and fires nothing on the prevented branch, so the guard is satisfied structurally. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
